self_consumption.explanation: Share of a plug-in system's output used at home rather than sent to the grid. Without a battery, power produced while nothing is running flows to the grid, which these laws generally do not pay for.
self_consumption.method: HTW Berlin Stecker-Solar-Simulator (web app, accessed 2026-11-10), 800 W system, no battery, panels vertical (90°) facing south, no shade, German weather and household load profiles. 'Nutzungsgrad' (share of solar output used on site) = avoided grid purchase / generation: 2,100 kWh/yr household 311/552 kWh = 56%; 3,000 kWh/yr 381/552 kWh = 69%; 5,000 kWh/yr 488/552 kWh = 88%. We use the 3,000 kWh case as 'typical' because it is under half the average US household's use (10,499 kWh/yr, EIA Form 861M, Sep 2025-Aug 2026) and below every state's average (lowest: California, 6,082 kWh/yr), so it leans conservative for most US homes.
self_consumption.limits: German weather and load profiles; vertical panels (tilted panels produce more at midday, so a smaller share may be used at home); 800 W system. Your own share depends on what runs in your home while the sun shines.
